games.title: Dandy
games.note: A four-player dungeon game for Atari 8-bit computers.

games.title: Gauntlet
games.note: Up to four players at once. It was first called Dungeons.

games.title: Paradroid
games.note: You take over enemy robots by winning a timed circuit puzzle.

games.title: Uridium
games.note: A fast scrolling shooter over the hulls of giant enemy dreadnoughts.

games.title: Knight Lore
games.dev: Ultimate Play the Game (Tim & Chris Stamper)
games.note: Its creators said they held it back for a year so it would not hurt sales of Sabre Wulf.

games.title: Sabre Wulf
games.note: Sabreman's first adventure, a jungle maze hunt for pieces of an amulet.

games.title: Batman (1986)
games.note: Batman must find the scattered parts of his Batcraft in an isometric maze of rooms.

games.title: Head over Heels
games.note: Players switch between two heroes, Head and Heels, who can join together into one.

games.title: Fairlight
games.note: Swedish programmer Bo Jangeborg wrote his own isometric engine for it.

games.title: Marble Madness
games.note: Designer Mark Cerny later led the hardware design of the PlayStation 4 and 5.

games.title: Super Monkey Ball
games.note: Players tilt the whole stage to roll a monkey in a ball to the goal.

games.title: Spindizzy
games.note: Players steer a spinning probe called GERALD around an isometric world of ramps and lifts.

games.title: The Sumerian Game
games.note: Designed by fourth-grade teacher Mabel Addis, called the first female video game designer and the first video game writer.

games.title: Hamurabi
games.note: David Ahl's best-selling 1973 book 101 BASIC Computer Games spread it to early home programmers.

games.title: Santa Paravia en Fiumaccio
games.note: Players rule a Renaissance Italian city-state, building markets, mills and cathedrals to rise in rank.

games.title: The Oregon Trail
games.dev: Don Rawitsch, Bill Heinemann & Paul Dillenberger
games.note: Three Carleton College students made it for a Minneapolis classroom. It ran on teleprinters with no graphics.

games.title: The Oregon Trail (1985)
games.note: The graphical Apple II version many American students played at school.

games.title: Organ Trail
games.dev: The Men Who Wear Many Hats
games.note: Began as a free Flash browser game. A Director's Cut followed on phones and Steam.

games.title: Hunt the Wumpus
games.note: Gregory Yob built its caves as a network instead of a grid because he was tired of 10-by-10 grid games.

games.title: M.U.L.E.
games.note: Four players colonize a planet, then compete in real-time auctions for food, energy and ore.

games.title: Offworld Trading Company
games.note: An economic real-time strategy game where you win by buying out rivals' stock instead of fighting.

games.title: Pikmin
games.note: Players lead swarms of small plant creatures to recover the parts of a crashed spaceship.

games.title: Archon
games.note: A chess-like board where each capture is fought out as a real-time arcade battle.

games.title: Empire (1977)
games.note: A turn-based world conquest game. A commercial version, Empire: Wargame of the Century, followed in 1987.

games.title: Utopia
games.note: Two players each rule an island, building farms, housing and forts as timed rounds tick by.

games.title: Raid on Bungeling Bay
games.note: Will Wright's first game: a helicopter bombing raid on factories spread across islands.

games.title: Little Computer People
games.note: Each copy created a unique little resident who lived in a house inside your computer.

links.took: Four-player dungeon crawling, which Ed Logg drew from Dandy.
links.added: Arcade co-op with a narrator, food to grab and heroes with set strengths.
links.extra: Dandy's author threatened legal action, and the dispute was settled without a lawsuit.

links.took: Andrew Braybrook's Graftgold design, straight after Paradroid.
links.added: Fast horizontal scrolling over giant metal dreadnoughts.

links.took: Isometric flip-screen rooms in Knight Lore's Filmation style.
links.added: Batman hunting Batcraft parts, with Bernie Drummond's art.

links.took: The isometric adventure style that other studios struggled to copy.
links.added: Bo Jangeborg's own engine, with objects you can push and stack.

links.took: Sabreman, Ultimate's pith-helmeted explorer.
links.added: Isometric 3D rooms and a werewolf curse to cure within 40 days.

links.took: Jon Ritman and Bernie Drummond's isometric engine and art style.
links.added: Two linked heroes who split up and combine to solve rooms.

links.took: Guiding a ball through tricky courses against the clock.
links.added: Tilting the whole stage, monkeys in balls and party minigames.

src.t: Wikipedia: Marble Madness, citing Retro Gamer and Gamasutra, 2008

links.took: Steering a rolling craft around an isometric course.
links.added: A large isometric world to map, with jewels to collect.

src.t: Wikipedia: Marble Madness, citing Retro Gamer, 2008

links.took: Running an ancient city's grain, land and people through typed commands.
links.added: A short program anyone could type in, first in FOCAL, later in BASIC.

links.took: Hamurabi's yearly decisions about grain, land and taxes.
links.added: City building: markets, mills and cathedrals that raise your rank.

src.t: Wikipedia: Hamurabi, citing Richard Moss, Ars Technica, 2015

links.took: Economic simulation, as critics like Jerry Pournelle noted.
links.added: Four players competing in real time, with auctions and a land grab.

src.t: Wikipedia: M.U.L.E., citing Jerry Pournelle, BYTE, 1984

links.took: A board-game model, chosen because it gets players dealing with each other.
links.added: Real-time auctions, planet colonizing and robot mules for four players.

src.t: Wikipedia: M.U.L.E., citing Dani Bunten, Computer Gaming World, April 1984

links.took: The Wumpus, which M.U.L.E. players can hunt in the mountains for cash.
links.added: A full trading game where the Wumpus hunt is a small side bonus.

links.took: Land claims, auctions and adjacency bonuses, per designer Soren Johnson.
links.added: Real-time stock buyouts on Mars instead of combat.

src.t: Soren Johnson, Designer Notes podcast, episode 18

links.took: Miyamoto named M.U.L.E. as an influence. The source doesn't say which part.
links.added: Leading swarms of plant creatures to collect ship parts in a garden-sized world.

src.t: Wikipedia: M.U.L.E., citing a Shigeru Miyamoto interview, 4Gamer

links.took: Asymmetric match-ups and one-on-one battles on a strategy map.
links.added: Space combat between fourteen alien ship designs, each with its own weapons.
links.extra: Co-designer Paul Reiche III described it as 3D space combat with the asymmetric match-ups of Archon.

links.took: City building and military conquest. Shelley listed twelve fixes he would make to Empire.
links.added: Technology, diplomacy and history from ancient times to the space age.

src.t: Wikipedia: Civilization (video game), citing Ars Technica

links.extra: Sid Meier and Bruce Shelley discussed their love of the original Empire before building the Civilization prototype.

links.took: The fun of building something up, and SimCity-like zoning in the prototype.
links.added: Whole civilizations competing on a world map across history.

src.t: Wikipedia: Civilization (video game), citing Benj Edwards, Gamasutra, 2007

links.took: A sweep of history and a technology chart like the board game's.
links.added: A full world map, conquest and computer rivals.
links.extra: Meier said the board game influenced him less than Empire or SimCity; MicroProse later licensed its name.

links.took: Building and managing a society, which GameSpot says laid SimCity's foundation.
links.added: A whole city with zoning, traffic and budgets, and no opponent.
links.extra: A critic's claim. No developer statement links the two games.

links.took: Managing a nation's growth. GameSpot called Utopia 'Civilization 0.5'.
links.added: A whole world, technology across history and many rival civilizations.

links.took: Will Wright's island level editor, which he enjoyed more than the game itself.
links.added: A city that grows on its own in response to zoning, roads and taxes.

src.t: Game Developer, GDC 2011: Wright talks Raid on Bungeling Bay origins

links.took: Watching a little person live a daily routine inside a house.
links.added: Families you direct, with careers, relationships and house building.
links.extra: Will Wright mentioned playing it and got feedback on The Sims from its designer, Rich Gold.

links.took: The wagon journey west, hunting, river crossings and disease.
links.added: Color graphics and a redesign for home Apple II users.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Oregon Trail (1971 video game)

links.took: Its trail structure and look. The first version was a straight parody.
links.added: A zombie apocalypse road trip in a station wagon.
